narrative: Material PL1__M2DE263B exhibits lumpy demand (CV=0.532, 93% non-zero days) with a near-normal distribution and no statistically significant trend. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.456) with a bimodal pattern suggesting two supplier delivery modes. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy is selected because it efficiently handles variable lead times and lumpy demand through a fixed reorder point trigger, while the EOQ batch size (4,233 units) reduces costly frequent replenishments from ~92 to ~28 orders/year, delivering 33.9% total cost savings.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) Continuous Review Reorder Point with EOQ
research_insights.selection_rationale: Lumpy but moderately high-volume demand with variable lead times favours continuous-review (r,Q) over periodic review. The EOQ provides the cost-optimal batch size while the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty at the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Capacity utilisation at 67% (5,378 of 8,028 units) leaves comfortable 2,650-unit headroom. No capacity constraint binds.
